newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says OECD affirms its policy direction.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says OECD affirms its policy direction.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) report on Germany backs the Bonn government's economic and fiscal policies, Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said.
Their remarks were contained in a joint statement.

"Now, the structural and austerity measures that have already been decided must be steadily implemented, without the unnecessary delays sought by state and local governments. That is also the view of the OECD," the ministers said.
The German government's view that an economic upturn will take hold this year and strengthen next year is affirmed by the OECD, despite small differences of interpretation, the statement said.
The OECD shares the German government's view that more flexibility and deregulation of the labour market is needed to eliminate structural bottlenecks.

The OECD projection of the German federal deficit being 3.4 percent of GDP for 1997 reflected only a small part of the austerity measures that have been decided by the government, the statement said. The OECD itself recognised this in its report.
